source_type_decision.reason: Both restored rows are the same Java OOP concept question. A correct answer must define and connect encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism, then distinguish their language mechanisms and engineering boundaries.

primary_sources_checked.title: Java Language Specification SE 25, 6.6 Access Control
verified_claims: Java access control is intended to prevent users of packages/classes from depending on unnecessary implementation details
accessibility is a compile-time property controlled by declarations and context

primary_sources_checked.title: Java Language Specification SE 25, 8.1.4 Superclasses and Subclasses
verified_claims: Object has no direct superclass; ordinary classes have a single direct superclass type, explicit or Object by default

primary_sources_checked.title: Java Language Specification SE 25, 8.4.8 Inheritance, Overriding, and Hiding
verified_claims: eligible superclass methods are inherited subject to accessibility/signature rules
instance-method overriding and class/static-method hiding are different language relationships

primary_sources_checked.title: Java Language Specification SE 25, 8.4.9 Overloading
verified_claims: same-name methods with non-override-equivalent signatures are overloaded and method applicability/selection is a compile-time concern

primary_sources_checked.title: Java Language Specification SE 25, 15.12.4.4 Locate Method to Invoke
verified_claims: static invocation needs no target reference and overriding is not allowed
ordinary virtual/interface calls can use dynamic method lookup starting from the target object's actual run-time class
private methods do not go through ordinary overriding lookup

primary_sources_checked.title: Java Language Specification SE 25, Chapter 9 Interfaces
verified_claims: a class may directly implement one or more interfaces
interface method modifiers include public/private, abstract/default/static, so interfaces are not restricted to abstract method declarations

findings.finding: The candidate answers both restored source rows directly and gives each of encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism a distinct purpose, mechanism and design boundary.
Runtime polymorphism is correctly bounded to overridable virtual/interface instance-method dispatch; overloading, static hiding and field access are explicitly kept out of that mechanism.
The answer uses Java SE 25 interface semantics and avoids the obsolete statement that interfaces can contain only abstract methods.
Composition-over-inheritance is presented as coupling/subtype-contract guidance rather than as a Java specification rule or unsupported performance guarantee.
